vulnerability.title: Disable Kernel Parameter for Accepting Source-Routed Packets on all IPv4 Interfaces
vulnerability.description: To set the runtime status of the net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_source_route kernel parameter, run the following command: $ sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_source_route=0 To make sure that the setting is persistent, add the following line to a file in the directory /etc/sysctl.d: net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_source_route = 0
vulnerability.recommendation: Remediation script: # Remediation is applicable only in certain platforms if rpm --quiet -q kernel-core; then # Comment out any occurrences of net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_source_route from /etc/sysctl.d/*.conf files for f in /etc/sysctl.d/*.conf /run/sysctl.d/*.conf /usr/local/lib/sysctl.d/*.conf; do # skip systemd-sysctl symlink (/etc/sysctl.d/99-sysctl.conf -> /etc/sysctl.conf) if [[ "$(readlink -f "$f")" == "/etc/sysctl.conf" ]]; then continue; fi matching_list=$(grep -P '^(?!#).*[\s]*net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_source_route.*$' $f | uniq ) if ! test -z "$matching_list"; then while IFS= read -r entry; do escaped_entry=$(sed -e 's|/|\\/|g' <<< "$entry") # comment out "net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_source_route" matches to preserve user data sed -i --follow-symlinks "s/^${escaped_entry}$/# &/g" $f done <<< "$matching_l
vulnerability.group: Network Related Kernel Runtime Parameters for Hosts and Routers

triage_decision.reason: Disabling accept_source_route is a standard network hardening step that does not affect authentication, authorization, or filesystem integrity. The change can be applied at runtime and made persistent via a sysctl.d file without requiring a reboot.

review_feedback: Setting net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_source_route to 0 drops source-routed packets, which includes most inbound traffic from external networks, breaking connectivity for services like SSH.

previous_review_verdicts.feedback: Plan would effectively disable accept_source_route but could be improved for robustness and to avoid duplicates.
concerns: Does not handle commented-out entries; may leave commented lines that could be re-enabled.
May create duplicate entries across multiple sysctl.d files if parameter already present.
Missing sudo prefix for sysctl command; may fail if not run as root.
No verification step after changes to confirm setting applied.
suggested_improvements: Comment out any existing occurrences of the parameter before adding a new line to ensure a single active setting.
Use a dedicated sysctl.d file with a high prefix (e.g., 99-disable-source-route.conf) and ensure it is the only source.
Run the sysctl command with sudo or ensure the script executes with root privileges.
After modifications, run `sysctl --system` to reload all sysctl settings and verify with `sysctl net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_source_route`.
